original_question: For integers k>3 and t in the currently unresolved range k+1 <= t <= 2(k-1)!, let P be a smallest family of permutations of [n] that t-shatters every k-subset of [n]. Determine whether there are values of t for which the minimum possible size of P does not lie in one of the three known regimes: exactly t, Theta(log log n), or Theta(log n).
target_in_paper: Section 14, first bullet-point open question immediately after Theorem 14.2: "Are there any values of t for which the size of an extremal family is not in one of these three regimes?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant section, the right objects (families of permutations of [n] that t-shatter every k-subset), the unresolved interval k+1 <= t <= 2(k-1)!, and the fact that the paper has three known regimes coming from the preceding theorems. It is therefore very close to the first open question stated in Section 14. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))
missing_details: The extremal quantity should be written explicitly as a function of n, for example f_k(n,t) = min{|P| : P ⊆ S_n and P t-shatters every k-subset of [n]}; there is no single family P independent of n. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

The draft should define [n] = {1, ..., n}, S_n as the symmetric group on [n], and 'P t-shatters X' as meaning that the restrictions of the permutations in P induce at least t distinct linear orders on X. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

The asymptotic notation should be made explicit: the question concerns the order of growth of the minimum as n -> infinity, with k and t fixed. This is implicit in the theorem statements but not stated in the draft. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

To match the paper exactly, the question should be tied to Theorem 14.2's known ranges: t = 1,2 gives size t; 3 <= t <= k gives Theta(log log n); and 2(k-1)! + 1 <= t <= k! gives Theta(log n). ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

The paper phrases this as the first of two open questions after Theorem 14.2; your draft captures only that first bullet and omits the separate conditional threshold question about where the Theta(log log n)-to-Theta(log n) transition occurs. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))

There is no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition here; those categories are not applicable because this is a pure extremal problem on permutation families. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))
refined_question: For fixed integers k > 3 and t with k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)!, let f_k(n,t) := min{|P| : P ⊆ S_n and, for every k-subset X ⊆ [n], the restrictions of the permutations in P to X realize at least t distinct orders}. Theorem 14.2 states that f_k(n,t) = t for t in {1,2}, f_k(n,t) = Theta(log log n) for 3 <= t <= k, and f_k(n,t) = Theta(log n) for 2(k - 1)! + 1 <= t <= k!. Does there exist any t in the unresolved interval k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)! for which f_k(n,t) is not in one of these three regimes, as n -> infinity? ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
justification: Section 14 first introduces shattering and t-shattering for families P ⊆ S_n, then records the complete k = 3 classification in Theorem 14.1 and the partial k > 3 classification in Theorem 14.2. Immediately afterward, the paper says that the unknown range is t in [k+1, 2(k-1)!] and asks, as its first bullet, exactly whether some such t yields an extremal family size outside the three previously seen regimes. That is the precise target your draft is aiming at; the rewrite above only makes the hidden notation and asymptotic quantifiers explicit so the question is stand-alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))
